Corner three-point shots exploit geometric advantages (shorter distance) and spatial constraints (defender spacing). Their efficiency arises from a non-linear trade-off between shot probability and point value, creating a local maximum around 22-24 feet. Defenses face a fundamental dilemma: Overplaying the corner frees up midrange or paint opportunities, while helping at the rim leaves the corner open. This generates a zero-sum game where optimal defense requires probabilistic coverage, leading to the observed 'anchored waiver' strategy. Mathematically, the primitives form a closed loop: Expected point value dictates offensive priority, which shapes defensive response cost, which influences strategic positioning, which ultimately determines shot efficiency gradient.
